analysis: Examined the head text of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 998-2059), the new ReasoningStopScope.swift, and the EngineV2BridgeTests changes. The PR threads a new stopStringScope argument into bridge.submitTokenized on the text path (lines 1043-1044) and the native MiMo media path (1426-1428). The vision path also gets a reasoningPrefix computed before submit (patch hunks at ~789-823). The stop-string matching scope, and so the point where generation ends, depends on the reasoning parser format and the think-open prompt state. The scope excludes <think>...</think> and tool-call spans from client stop-string matching. Security impact is limited to output-truncation semantics and an availability or correctness improvement. It does not touch the coordinator-to-provider crypto path (TB-002), attestation, authorization, or key handling. It does not touch the prefix-cache name derivation, TTL, or salt scoping (T-041); cacheScope and cacheEnabled are passed through unchanged. Stop strings come from the consumer request, but they only end the consumer's own request and do not cross tenants. The scope enum is a pure function with no I/O, no logging, and no new data stored at rest. Cancellation and release paths (releaseBox.fire, bridge.cancel) around the changed region are unchanged. Remaining gaps are outside the supplied evidence. CBv2StopStringScope and EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence were not visible, so I could not verify the scope state machine's edge cases, such as a model-emitted <think> marker used to suppress stops, or its memory bounds on long holdback. The vision-path hunk was only partly visible, because its patch excerpt was truncated. The test-file changes are test-only. No concrete security regression was identified.
